_: Curated inventory expansion for the five destinations closest to the category threshold. Every entry is a real, long-established, independently verifiable venue that we do not already hold, chosen because a traveler browsing that city would expect to find it. Nothing here is invented, nothing is a chain filler, and nothing was copied from another review site: the names are the venues' own, and every attribute they end up carrying comes from OpenStreetMap through the existing enricher, which refuses a match it cannot verify. Deduplication happens on the same normalised (destination, name) key the places table is unique on, so re-running this changes nothing.
_threshold: The category threshold stays at 6. These were chosen to let real inventory reach it, not to reach it by any means: each city gets the venues that were genuinely missing rather than the minimum number that would tip the count.

places.name: Ancient Agora of Athens
places.why: The civic centre of classical Athens and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Missing from a list that already holds the Acropolis and four museums.

places.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
places.why: One of the four sites on the Athens combined ticket we already describe elsewhere.

places.name: Benaki Museum of Greek Culture
places.why: The major Greek cultural collection outside the state museums.

places.name: British Museum
places.why: The most visited museum in the country and absent from our London list.

places.name: Tower of London
places.why: Historic royal palace and the single most obvious London omission after the British Museum.

places.name: National Gallery
places.why: Free national collection on Trafalgar Square.

places.name: Rembrandt House Museum
places.why: Rembrandt's own house and studio, a short walk from the Rijksmuseum we already cover.

places.name: Royal Palace of Amsterdam
places.why: The seventeenth-century town hall on Dam Square, open to visitors.

places.name: NEMO Science Museum
places.why: The city's science museum, and the one attraction on this list a family would look for.

places.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
places.why: The largest art museum in the Americas, and a conspicuous gap next to the Whitney.

places.name: American Museum of Natural History
places.why: The other museum every first-time visitor asks about.

places.name: Museum of Modern Art
places.why: MoMA. Distinct from the Whitney and from the Met, and separately ticketed.

places.name: Musee d'Orsay
places.why: The impressionist collection, and the museum most often visited alongside the Louvre we already hold.

places.name: Arc de Triomphe
places.why: Monument with a paid rooftop terrace, comparable to the Eiffel Tower entry we already have.

places.name: Centre Pompidou
places.why: The modern art museum. Its building closes for renovation, which is exactly the kind of fact a place page should carry.

places.name: Bouillon Chartier
places.why: An 1896 bouillon still serving at bouillon prices, and the counterweight to the expensive brasseries we already list.

places.name: Le Train Bleu
places.why: The Gare de Lyon dining room, a listed historic monument.

places.name: Chez L'Ami Jean
places.why: A long-running Basque bistro in the 7th, and a different price band from Le Procope and Brasserie Lipp.
